title: Why Abe Lincoln Grew a Beard
titleZh: 亚伯·林肯为什么留起了胡子

q.en: Who was Grace Bedell, and where did she live?
q.zh: 格雷丝·贝德尔(Grace Bedell)是谁？她住在哪里？

options.en: Abraham Lincoln's wife
options.zh: 亚伯拉罕·林肯的妻子

options.en: A president's daughter who lived in Washington, D.C., and wrote letters to the White House every single week of her father's term
options.zh: 一位住在华盛顿特区的美国总统的女儿，在父亲任期里每个星期都给白宫写信

options.en: A famous painter who drew Lincoln
options.zh: 一位为林肯画像的著名画家

options.en: An eleven-year-old girl from western New York who suggested Lincoln grow a beard
options.zh: 一个来自纽约州西部、建议林肯留胡子的十一岁女孩

explain.en: The book says an 'eleven-year-old girl living in western New York' named Grace Bedell decided Lincoln should grow a beard and wrote to tell him so.
explain.zh: 书里说，一个「住在纽约州西部的十一岁女孩」格雷丝·贝德尔认为林肯应该留胡子，并写信这样告诉他。

q.en: In her letter, what did Grace tell Lincoln a beard would do for his campaign?
q.zh: 在信里，格雷丝告诉林肯，胡子会对他的竞选起到什么作用？

options.en: Keep him warm during the winter, since he traveled by open train through the snowy North and caught cold at every stop
options.zh: 让他在冬天保暖，因为他乘敞篷火车穿越白雪覆盖的北方，每停一站都要感冒

options.en: Make ladies like him, so they would urge their husbands to vote for him
options.zh: 让女士们喜欢他，从而怂恿丈夫把票投给他

options.en: Make him look much younger
options.zh: 让他看起来年轻很多

options.en: Help him hear speeches better
options.zh: 帮他更好地听演讲

explain.en: Grace wrote: 'All the ladies like whiskers and they would tease their husbands to vote for you and then you would be President.' She also said she would get her brothers to vote for him.
explain.zh: 格雷丝写道：「所有女士都喜欢胡子，她们会缠着丈夫投你一票，这样你就能当总统了。」她还说会拉兄弟们也投他。

q.en: In his reply, what did Lincoln say about his own children?
q.zh: 在回信里，林肯怎样形容自己的孩子？

options.en: He had no daughters, but three sons aged seventeen, nine, and seven
options.zh: 他没有女儿，但有三个儿子，分别十七岁、九岁和七岁

options.en: He had only one son
options.zh: 他只有一个儿子

options.en: He had no children at all, and the White House stayed silent without any family noise during his entire time as president
options.zh: 他根本没有孩子，在他当总统的整个期间，白宫因为没有家人而一片寂静

options.en: He had four daughters
options.zh: 他有四个女儿

explain.en: Lincoln wrote, 'I have no daughters. I have three sons—one seventeen, one nine, and one seven years of age.' (Grace had asked if he had daughters her age.)
explain.zh: 林肯写道：「我没有女儿。我有三个儿子——一个十七岁、一个九岁、一个七岁。」（格雷丝曾问过他有没有和她同岁的女儿。）

q.en: What happened when Lincoln's train stopped in Westfield, New York?
q.zh: 当林肯的火车停在纽约州韦斯特菲尔德(Westfield)时，发生了什么？

options.en: He refused to meet anyone
options.zh: 他拒绝见任何人

options.en: He met Grace, said 'look at my whiskers, I've been growing them for you,' and kissed her cheek
options.zh: 他见到了格雷丝，说「看我的胡子，我是为了你才留的」，并亲了她的脸颊

options.en: He shaved off his beard
options.zh: 他把自己的胡子剃掉了

options.en: He gave a long speech about the war, explaining to the crowd gathered at the station why the beard had helped him win the election and end the fighting
options.zh: 他向聚在车站的人群发表了一篇关于战争的长篇演说，解释这胡子怎样帮他赢下大选、结束战事

explain.en: In Grace's hometown, Lincoln asked for 'the young lady who wrote the letter.' He told her, 'Gracie, look at my whiskers. I have been growing them for you,' and gave her a kiss on the cheek.
explain.zh: 在格雷丝的家乡，林肯要见「写那封信的小姑娘」。他对她说：「格雷西，看我的胡子。我是为了你才留的」，并亲了亲她的脸颊。

q.en: In the book, what does the word 'whiskers' mean?
q.zh: 在书中，「whiskers」这个词是什么意思？

options.en: Another word people used back then for a beard
options.zh: 当时人们用来指「胡子」的另一个词

options.en: A kind of mustache only, the small strip of hair some men wore above the lip in Lincoln's time and called by that very word
options.zh: 仅指一种胡子（八字胡），即林肯时代有些男人在上唇上方留的那一小撮，而且就用这个词来称呼

options.en: A type of hat
options.zh: 一种帽子

options.en: A vote in an election
options.zh: 选举中的一张选票

explain.en: The book explains, 'Back then, beards were often called whiskers.' Grace and Lincoln both use 'whiskers' to mean a beard.
explain.zh: 书里解释：「那时候，胡子常被叫做 whiskers。」格雷丝和林肯都用 whiskers 来指胡子。

q.en: A side note says the 19th Amendment was ratified in 1920. What did it do?
q.zh: 书里的旁注说第十九条修正案于 1920 年批准生效。它做了什么？

options.en: It ended the Civil War
options.zh: 它结束了南北战争

options.en: It elected Abraham Lincoln, putting the first bearded man in the White House
options.zh: 它选举了亚伯拉罕·林肯，把第一位留胡子的人送进了白宫

options.en: It made beards illegal
options.zh: 它规定留胡子违法

options.en: It gave women the right to vote
options.zh: 它赋予了女性投票权

explain.en: The side note says, 'Women struggled for many years to achieve the right to vote. They weren't allowed to vote until 1920, when the 19th Amendment was ratified.' Grace wrote in 1860 that she wished she could vote.
explain.zh: 旁注写道：「女性奋斗多年才争取到投票权。她们直到 1920 年第十九条修正案批准时才被允许投票。」格雷丝在 1860 年写信说，如果自己是男人就会投他一票。

q.en: According to Grace, why would growing a beard help Lincoln become president?
q.zh: 根据格雷丝的说法，留胡子为什么会帮林肯当上总统？

options.en: Because it scared his opponents away
options.zh: 因为那能把对手吓跑

options.en: Because the law required every candidate to have a beard, and Lincoln would have faced a fine each morning he showed up clean-shaven
options.zh: 因为法律规定每位候选人都必须留胡子，林肯若哪天早上刮了脸露面，就得挨一笔罚款

options.en: Because ladies liked whiskers and would push their husbands to vote for him
options.zh: 因为女士们喜欢胡子，会去说服丈夫投他

options.en: Because it made him look like a soldier
options.zh: 因为那让他看起来像个军人

explain.en: Grace reasoned that 'all the ladies like whiskers' and would 'tease their husbands to vote for you.' She connected a beard to winning votes, especially from women's influence.
explain.zh: 格雷丝的逻辑是「所有女士都喜欢胡子」，会「缠着丈夫投你一票」。她把留胡子与赢得选票——尤其是通过女性影响丈夫——联系了起来。

q.en: What does the book say about Lincoln and the presidents who came before him?
q.zh: 关于林肯和他之前的各位总统，书里是怎么说的？

options.en: He was the very first president of the United States
options.zh: 他是美国第一任总统

options.en: All 15 presidents before him had full beards, and several even wore longer ones than Lincoln ever did, which is why his clean-shaven face looked so unusual at first
options.zh: 他之前的 15 位总统都留着满脸胡子，其中几位留得比林肯还长，所以林肯那张干净无胡的脸起初看着格外怪

options.en: He was the 10th president of the United States
options.zh: 他是美国第 10 任总统

options.en: Lincoln was the 16th president and the first to grow a full beard; none of the 15 before him even had a mustache
options.zh: 林肯是第 16 任总统，也是第一位留满胡子的；之前的 15 位连八字胡都没有

explain.en: The book states Lincoln 'was the first president to grow a full beard. None of the fifteen presidents who came before him even had a mustache.' He was the 16th president.
explain.zh: 书里说林肯「是第一位留满胡子的总统。在他之前的十五位总统连八字胡都没有。」他是第 16 任总统。

q.en: Why does the author tell the story of a child's letter to the president?
q.zh: 作者为什么要讲述一个小孩给总统写信的故事？

options.en: To argue that presidents should never listen to children, because young ideas are too silly to matter, only grown men should decide the country's future, and Grace's letter was a mistake the president ought to have ignored
options.zh: 为了论证总统绝不该听孩子的话，因为孩子的想法太幼稚、无足轻重，只有成年男子才该决定国家的前途，而格雷丝那封信本是总统本该无视的一个错误

options.en: To explain how postage stamps are made
options.zh: 为了解释邮票是怎么印出来的

options.en: To teach readers how to grow a beard
options.zh: 为了教读者怎么留胡子

options.en: To show that one child's suggestion can influence history, and that letters let ordinary people reach their leaders
options.zh: 为了说明一个孩子的一个建议也能影响历史，而且信件能让普通人联系到他们的领袖

explain.en: The book frames Grace's letter as 'one such child, one such suggestion, and one of our most famous presidents'—showing how a child's idea reached the president and became part of history.
explain.zh: 书把格雷丝的信描述成「这样一个孩子、这样一个建议，以及我们最著名的总统之一」——说明一个孩子的想法如何传达到总统耳中，并成了历史的一部分。

q.en: Why is there a statue of Lincoln and Grace in Westfield, New York?
q.zh: 为什么纽约州韦斯特菲尔德会有一座林肯和格雷丝的雕像？

options.en: To remember the real meeting between the girl whose letter led to his beard and the president-elect
options.zh: 为了纪念那位用信件促成他留胡子的女孩与当选总统之间真实的一次会面

options.en: Because Lincoln was born there
options.zh: 因为林肯出生在那里

options.en: Because Grace later became president herself, the first woman to hold the office and the one who finally built the statue to mark the meeting she had caused
options.zh: 因为格雷丝后来自己当上了总统，是第一位担任此职的女性，也正是她最终建起那座雕像，来纪念由她引发的会面

options.en: Because it is where Lincoln died
options.zh: 因为那是林肯去世的地方

explain.en: At Lincoln-Bedell Statue Park in Westfield, two bronze statues 'capture the historic meeting' between president-elect Lincoln and Grace Bedell, erected in 1999.
explain.zh: 在韦斯特菲尔德的林肯-贝德尔雕像公园，两座青铜雕像「定格了当选总统林肯与格雷丝·贝德尔那次历史性的会面」，于 1999 年落成。

prompt.en: Grace, an eleven-year-old, wrote a letter that may have changed history by convincing Lincoln to grow a beard. Think of a time you shared an idea or suggestion with an adult. Did it make a difference? Why is it brave to share your opinion, even as a child?
prompt.zh: 十一岁的格雷丝写了一封信，可能改变了历史——她说服了林肯留胡子。回想一次你向大人提出想法或建议的经历。它起作用了吗？为什么即使还是孩子，敢于说出自己的看法也是一种勇敢？

en: Grace wrote to Lincoln on October 15, 1860, suggesting he grow 'whiskers' to win votes (p. 7-9).
Lincoln later met her in Westfield and said, 'I have been growing them for you' (p. 12-13).
A good answer connects a personal experience of speaking up to the idea that one voice—even a child's—can matter.
zh: 格雷丝在 1860 年 10 月 15 日写信给林肯，建议他留「胡子」来赢得选票（第7-9页）。
后来林肯在韦斯特菲尔德见到她，说：「我是为了你才留的」（第12-13页）。
好的回答会把一次「勇敢发声」的个人经历，和「哪怕是孩子，一个声音也很重要」这个想法联系起来。
